title: An enum body that starts with a lone comma (enum E { , } or { ,; ... }) is rejected by scalac's Java parser
oracle: javac accepts the Java source; scalac's Java parser must accept it too
generator: wave4/harness/javaparser (gen.py, Driver.scala), feature E (empty enum body forms; the comma forms were taken out of the generator after this finding to quiet later runs)
signature: SRC-ERROR ERROR: identifier expected but `,` found.
detail: JLS 8.9.1 allows a trailing comma after an empty list of enum constants, so `enum E0 { , }` and `enum E1 { ,; static int z() { return 1; } }` are valid and javac compiles them. scalac's Java parser reports 'identifier expected but `,` found' for both, because JavaParsers.enumDecl parses a constant whenever the body does not start with `;` or `}` and only then looks for a comma. A trailing comma after at least one constant (`A, B,;`) is accepted. Hand-written code does not do this; a code generator that always emits a separator could.
fix_sketch: In parseEnumConsts accept a comma before the first constant when the next token is `;` or `}`. No compatibility cost.
prior: none found (J4 to J9 are other wrong rejections by the same parser)
